definition: A server that sits between users and the internet and can filter or log traffic.
exampleSentence: The proxy server blocks access to risky websites for all employees.

definition: A firewall that filters and blocks harmful HTTP traffic aimed at web apps.
exampleSentence: A web application firewall blocked thousands of injection attempts every single day.

definition: A firewall that also inspects applications, users and threats, not only ports.
exampleSentence: The next-generation firewall can block a risky app even if it uses port 443.

definition: Running suspicious files in an isolated environment to watch what they do.
exampleSentence: Sandboxing showed that the invoice attachment tried to contact a strange server.

definition: A system that checks devices and decides whether they may join the network.
exampleSentence: NAC refused to connect the laptop because its antivirus was out of date.

definition: Limiting which devices may use a physical or switch port.
exampleSentence: Port security shut down the socket when an unknown laptop was plugged in.

definition: A list of approved items, such as apps or addresses, that are the only ones allowed.
exampleSentence: Only apps on the allowlist can run on the cash register computers.

definition: A list of items, such as addresses or domains, that are always denied.
exampleSentence: The mail filter added the sender to the blocklist after the third scam email.

definition: Software that finds and removes harmful programs from a device.
exampleSentence: The antimalware tool quarantined the file before anybody could open it.

definition: Security software and settings that protect laptops, phones and servers.
exampleSentence: Endpoint protection must be installed on every device before it joins the network.

definition: A service where outside experts monitor and respond to threats for a company.
exampleSentence: A small company without night staff can buy an MDR service for round-the-clock monitoring.

definition: Allowing only approved programs to run on a computer.
exampleSentence: Application whitelisting stopped the unknown installer from starting on the kiosk.

definition: Encrypting all data on a laptop or phone so a thief cannot read it.
exampleSentence: Device encryption protected our files when a laptop was stolen from the train.

definition: A startup feature that allows only trusted software to load when a computer starts.
exampleSentence: Secure boot refused to start the system after somebody changed the boot files.

definition: A chip in a computer that stores keys and checks that the system is trusted.
exampleSentence: The disk key is stored in the TPM, so it cannot be copied easily.

definition: Software that lets IT enforce security settings on company phones and tablets.
exampleSentence: Mobile device management lets us erase a lost phone from the office.

definition: Scanning incoming email to block spam, phishing and harmful attachments.
exampleSentence: Email filtering stops most scam messages before employees see them.

definition: Blocking access to dangerous websites at the DNS level.
exampleSentence: DNS filtering warned the user when she clicked a link to a known scam site.

definition: Blocking or allowing web content based on categories and rules.
exampleSentence: Content filtering prevents downloads from file sharing sites on the office network.

definition: Blocking traffic that comes from certain countries or regions.
exampleSentence: We use geo-blocking because our admin panel is never used outside the country.

definition: Constantly watching network traffic and devices to spot problems and attacks.
exampleSentence: Network monitoring alerted us when one server began to send huge amounts of data.

definition: Studying network traffic patterns to find unusual or harmful behavior.
exampleSentence: Traffic analysis showed that a device was sending data every sixty seconds.

definition: Examining the content of network packets, not only their headers.
exampleSentence: Deep packet inspection found hidden commands inside normal-looking web traffic.

definition: Applying separate security rules to each workload inside a data center or cloud.
exampleSentence: Microsegmentation means a hacked web server cannot talk to the payroll system.

definition: A controlled machine used to reach other servers in a secure zone.
exampleSentence: Every session on the jump server is recorded for later review.

definition: A process for reporting and publicly sharing information about a security flaw.
exampleSentence: The vendor published a vulnerability disclosure together with the fixed version.

definition: Controlling and limiting traffic that leaves a network.
exampleSentence: Egress filtering blocked the malware from contacting its remote server.

definition: Checking and limiting traffic that enters a network.
exampleSentence: Ingress filtering drops packets that claim to come from our own internal addresses.

definition: A rule that blocks everything unless it is specifically allowed.
exampleSentence: A default deny policy forces teams to ask before opening any new port.

definition: Settings chosen to reduce risk and remove unnecessary features from a system.
exampleSentence: A secure configuration guide is attached to every new server request.

definition: Rules that define which users and devices may reach which network resources.
exampleSentence: The network access policy says guests can only use the visitor Wi-Fi.

definition: A firewall that tracks active connections and allows only matching replies.
exampleSentence: A stateful firewall only accepts replies for connections that users started.

definition: Allowing or blocking network packets based on addresses, ports and protocols.
exampleSentence: Basic packet filtering at the router already blocks a lot of unwanted traffic.

definition: A tool that detects attacks in network traffic and blocks them automatically.
exampleSentence: The intrusion prevention system dropped the exploit before it reached the server.

definition: Removing unneeded features and tightening settings on laptops and servers.
exampleSentence: Endpoint hardening disabled macros and old protocols on every company laptop.

definition: Rules that decide which programs may run on a device.
exampleSentence: Application control prevented the downloaded tool from starting on the work laptop.

definition: Running web browsing in a separate environment so threats cannot reach the device.
exampleSentence: With browser isolation, a malicious page cannot touch the employee's computer.

definition: Preventing unapproved USB devices from connecting to company computers.
exampleSentence: USB blocking stopped a staff member from copying files to a personal drive.

definition: Services that absorb or filter huge floods of traffic aimed at a website.
exampleSentence: DDoS protection kept the shop online during the biggest attack of the year.

definition: Protecting the outer boundary of a network with firewalls and similar controls.
exampleSentence: Perimeter security alone is not enough when staff work from home.
